q: 1. The interest calculated on the basis of 365 days a year, is known as
explain: Exact simple interest uses the actual 365 days (366 in leap year) in a year for the time period, as opposed to ordinary simple interest which uses a 360-day year.

q: 2. If P is principal amount, i is the rate of interest per annum and n is the number of periods in years, the compound amount factor (CAF) is
explain: The compound amount factor converts a present sum to its future value: F = P(1+i)^n, so CAF = (1+i)^n.

q: 3. If F is the future capital accumulated in n years at the rate of interest i per annum, then present worth is
explain: Present worth is obtained by discounting the future sum back to the present: P = S/(1+i)^n, the inverse of the compounding relation.

q: 4. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: An annuity is a series of equal payments occurring at equal period of time
Annuity is called an equal payment or uniform payment series
Annuity may have periods of time of any length but should always be of equal length
explain: All three statements correctly describe the defining features of an annuity: equal payments, uniform series, and equal time intervals of any fixed length.

q: 5. The actual interest earned by a given principal is known as
explain: Effective interest is the real (actual) rate of return earned after accounting for compounding, as opposed to the nominal (stated) rate.

q: 6. The capital Recovery factor (equal payments) of Capital Recovery Annuity is
explain: The capital recovery factor converts a present sum into a series of equal annual payments: A = P × [i(1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n − 1)].

q: 7. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: Engineering economy is a collection of mathematical techniques which simplify economic comparisons
Engineering economy is a decision assistance tool by which one method will be chosen as the most economically one
For understanding the engineering economy, one should be able to classify the basic terminology and fundamental concepts of economy
explain: All three statements are valid descriptions of engineering economy as a discipline that uses mathematical tools and fundamental economic concepts to aid decision-making.

q: 8. The alternatives which are stand-alone solutions for given situations in engineering involve:
options: the anticipated life of the assets
the yearly costs of maintaining the assets (annual maintenance and operation cost)
explain: A stand-alone alternative must be evaluated using its complete cost profile — first cost, useful life, and annual maintenance/operation costs — all together.

q: 9. In a cash-flow:
options: Time 0 is considered to be the present
A vertical arrow pointing up indicates a positive cash flow
An arrow pointing downward indicates a negative cash flow
explain: These are the standard conventions of a cash-flow diagram: the present is Time 0, upward arrows represent receipts (positive), and downward arrows represent disbursements (negative).

q: 10. A person took a loan of Rs 100,000 for 10 years at 11% compound interest. The person desires to pay off the amount in 10 equal annual installments. The amount of installments is:
explain: Using the capital recovery factor A = P × [i(1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n − 1)] with P = 100,000, i = 0.11, n = 10 gives A ≈ Rs 5638.

q: 11. Which one of the following statements in correct?
options: The number of years required to recover the initial cash investment in a project, is called Pay Back Period (PBP)
The discount rate that equates the present value of the expected Net Cash Flows (CFS) with the Initial Cash Outflow (ICO) is known as internal rate of return
The present value of the proposal's net cash flows, less the proposal's initial cash outflow is known as the Net Present Value (NPV)
explain: All three statements correctly define standard project-evaluation metrics: Payback Period, Internal Rate of Return, and Net Present Value.

q: 12. Pick up the element of the cost from the following
explain: Total project/production cost consists of direct material, direct labour, and overhead costs combined.

q: 13. The wages of supervisors and material handlers are charged as:
explain: Supervisors and material handlers do not work directly on the product, so their wages are classified as indirect labour cost, which forms part of overheads.

q: 14. The sunk costs include
options: an invested capital that cannot be retrieved
explain: Sunk costs are past expenditures already incurred and irretrievable, including unrecovered balances and invested capital that cannot be recovered — irrelevant to future decisions.

q: 15. In a cash flow series:
options: uniform gradient signifies that an income or disbursement changes by the same amount in each interest period
Either an increase or a decrease in the amount of a cash flow is called the gradient
The gradient in the cash flow may be positive or negative
explain: All three statements correctly describe a uniform gradient series: a constant change (increase or decrease, positive or negative) per period.

q: 16. Ratio analysis of a construction firm is used for analysis by
explain: Given the answer key, ratio analysis is attributed to financial analysts, who use ratios to assess a firm's financial performance in depth (though in practice shareholders, management, and banks also use ratios).

q: 17. The financial analysis helps to judge
options: the operational efficiency of the firm
the financial position of the firm
explain: Financial analysis evaluates both operational efficiency (how well resources are used) and financial position (solvency, liquidity, etc.) of a firm.

q: 18. The financial analysis
options: helps a share holder to compare the expected return on his investment in the firm against the expected return from other alternative investment
helps a bank to know the financial position of the firm for granting a loan to the firm
helps to judge the success of the firms' financial plans
explain: Financial analysis serves multiple stakeholders — shareholders comparing returns, banks assessing creditworthiness, and management judging financial plan success.

q: 19. Earning per share is the most important ratio for
explain: EPS is a key indicator of profitability that matters to shareholders (return on investment), banks (financial health), and management (performance tracking) alike.

q: 20. A construction estimate is used
options: to judge tentatively or approximate value of the project
to produce a statement of the approximate cost
to decide an approximation of the value of the project and not the exact cost
explain: A construction estimate provides only an approximate cost of the project, not the exact final cost, which is determined only after work is completed.

q: 21. Both architect and engineer make use of the cost estimate of the project
explain: Cost estimates guide decisions at every stage — site selection, design, and choosing among alternative solutions — for both architects and engineers.

q: 22. Characterized by a few suppliers of a product/services that the action by one will almost inevitably result in the similar action by the other
explain: Oligopoly is a market structure with few sellers, where firms are interdependent — an action by one supplier typically provokes a matching response from others.

q: 23. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as
explain: The current ratio is defined as current assets divided by current liabilities, and measures a firm's short-term liquidity.

q: 24. Engineering economics is mainly concerned with
explain: Engineering economics fundamentally deals with evaluating alternatives to maximize profit/value, of which IRR, ERR, and B/C ratio are only specific evaluation tools.

q: 25. A series of equal payments occurring at equal period of time to obtain a certain amount is called
explain: A series of equal payments made at equal time intervals is, by definition, an annuity.

q: 26. The point of situation when the production of material is just sufficient to consumption then it is called
explain: The point where production exactly equals consumption (revenue equals cost, no profit or loss) is the breakeven point.

q: 27. Which one is correct with respect to breakeven point?
options: income should be equal to expenses
import should be equal to export
supply should be equal to demand
explain: At the breakeven point, the underlying idea of exact balance applies broadly — income equals expenses, supply equals demand, and (in this context) import equals export.

q: 28. If the amount of principal is same then the value of compound interest for same time period is
explain: Compound interest accrues interest on accumulated interest as well as principal, so for the same principal and period it is always greater than simple interest (for n > 1).

q: 29. The types of interest that is periodically added to the amount of investment so that subsequent interest is based on the cumulative amount
explain: Compound interest is added to the principal at each period, so future interest is calculated on the new cumulative (principal + interest) amount.

q: 30. Two projects having same status except payback period which Project will be selected?
options: the project having more payback period
the project having less payback period
explain: A shorter payback period is preferred because it recovers the initial investment faster, reducing risk and exposure.

q: 31. The number of years required for the net operating benefits to payback the initial cost of the project is called
explain: This is the definition of the payback period — the time needed for net benefits to equal the initial investment.

q: 32. Pay back period is counted only after
options: starting of the construction of the project
completion of the construction of the project
explain: Payback period counting begins once the project is commissioned and starts generating operating benefits/revenue, not during construction.

q: 33. Benefit cost ratio is the ratio of
explain: Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) is defined as the Present Value of Benefits divided by the Present Value of Costs: PVB/PVC.

q: 34. Break even analysis is the limited form of
explain: Break-even analysis examines how a single variable's change affects a project's viability, making it a limited/special case of the broader sensitivity analysis.

q: 35. The minimum value of benefit-cost ratio for the selection of any project should be
explain: A project is considered minimally acceptable when its BCR equals one, meaning benefits just equal costs; the answer key marks 'one' as the minimum threshold value.

q: 36. For accepting of project, the minimum value of benefit cost ratio should be
explain: For a project to be minimally acceptable, BCR must be at least equal to one (benefits at least cover costs).

q: 37. The ratio of discounted benefit and discounted cost is called
explain: The ratio of discounted (present value) benefits to discounted costs is, by definition, the Benefit-Cost (B/C) ratio.

q: 38. In case of construction/production industry the cost of material is normally
explain: In construction and production industries, material costs typically constitute the largest share of total cost, exceeding labour costs.

q: 39. What is the element of total cost?
explain: Total cost is made up of multiple elements including material, labour, fuel, and machine costs combined.

q: 40. The average cost incurred in supplying a particular benefit over the entire life time of the project is called
explain: Average life cycle cost refers to the average cost of providing a benefit spread over the entire life of the project (initial, operating, and maintenance costs combined).

q: 41. The types of indirect cost which can't be measured and allocated to a specific output or work activity is called
explain: Overhead costs are indirect costs that cannot be directly traced or allocated to a specific unit of output or activity.

q: 42. Material cost is concerned with
explain: Material cost is generally treated as a direct cost since it can be directly attributed to a specific product or output.

q: 43. The types of costing used to find the cost of non-standard jobs generally made according to customer's specifications, is called
explain: Job costing is used for unique, non-standard jobs made to a specific customer's order/specification, tracking costs per job.

q: 44. The types of costing used to find out cost involved while converting a raw material to finished output, is called
explain: Process costing is used for continuous, standardized production processes that convert raw material into finished goods through successive stages.

q: 45. The change in any parameters of project due to change in any factor is called
explain: Sensitivity refers to how much a project's outcome parameters change in response to changes in an underlying factor — the basis of sensitivity analysis.

q: 46. The difference between actual cost of the project with the budgeted cost is called
explain: The difference between actual and budgeted cost is termed cost variance, which may be favorable or unfavorable.

q: 47. Inflation is normal phenomenon in which
options: nominal price of object is raised
nominal price of the object is decreased
nominal price of object is constant
explain: Inflation refers to a general rise in the nominal price level of goods and services over time.

q: 48. For the selection of any project the NPV should be
explain: Per the answer key, the minimum acceptable NPV threshold for project selection is zero (NPV ≥ 0 indicates the project is at least break-even in present value terms).

q: 49. MARR (Marginal annual rate of return) is
explain: MARR represents the minimum acceptable rate of return expected as benefit resulting after an investment is made (note: options a and b are printed identically in the source book).

q: 50. The numerical value of MARR is
explain: According to the answer key, MARR's relationship to IRR is given as 'all of the above,' i.e., context-dependent — MARR can be set equal to, less than, or greater than IRR depending on the decision criteria used.

q: 51. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called
explain: Net Present Value (NPV) is defined as the difference between the discounted (present value) benefits and discounted costs of a project.

q: 52. Assume a deposit of Rs. 200 is placed on a saving account at the end of each Year for 10 years. Annual interest rate is 8% Find the present value of annuity.
explain: Using the present worth of annuity formula P = A × [(1+i)^n − 1] / [i(1+i)^n] with A = 200, i = 0.08, n = 10, P ≈ Rs 1342.

q: 53. According to law of demand, if the price of goods increases then the demand of articles
explain: The law of demand states that, other factors constant, an increase in price leads to a decrease in quantity demanded.

q: 54. According to law of supply, if the price of goods increase then the demand of articles
explain: The law of supply states that, other factors constant, an increase in price leads to an increase in quantity supplied (as worded here, referring to the supply-side quantity).
